correctness.rationale: The propagation proof is complete in both directions. Starting at an extreme vertex in \(A_p\) monitors the entire \(B\)-side; successive \(B_i\) vertices then release the \(A_i\) twin classes precisely when the residual class sizes are at most \(k\), giving the condition \(L_A\le k\); the \(B_1\) argument is symmetric. Conversely, if a singleton lies in \(A_i\), any other unmonitored \(A_j\) of size greater than \(k\) permanently blocks propagation, and when \(i<p\) a too-large home class plus the next nonempty class blocks the first propagation step. Thus any successful singleton implies \(L_A\le k\), with the symmetric alternative on the other side. An extreme pair \(\{a,b\}\in A_p\times B_1\) dominates the graph immediately, so the minimum is always one or two. A fresh independent literal simulation over 765 canonical profiles/parameter choices through order nine agreed with the formula; the simulation is corroborative, not the infinite proof.
